  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-01",
  "sketch": {

    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Every analyst can read all customer emails, phones and purchase history",
      "scenario": "Any employee in the analyst group, or an attacker who phishes one analyst account, can query the full customer table in the warehouse. The copy contains direct identifiers and purchase history for the whole customer base, so one compromised or curious analyst exfiltrates bulk PII with a single SELECT. No need-to-know restriction or row/column scoping is described.",
      "component": "Analytics warehouse access model",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "All analysts have read access to the warehouse." },
        { "quote": "including email addresses, phone numbers and purchase history" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-1220", "CWE-359"],
      "plainLanguage": "Everyone on the analytics team can see every customer's email, phone number and what they bought, whether they need it or not.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict warehouse access to the customer data analysts actually need",
        "given": "the exported customers dataset exists in the analytics warehouse",
        "when": "an analyst queries it",
        "then": "access is granted per role or per dataset on a need-to-know basis and the broad all-analysts read grant on identifier columns is removed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Direct identifiers are exported in the clear instead of being masked or minimised",
      "scenario": "The job copies raw email addresses and phone numbers even though analytics usually needs behaviour, not contact details. This creates a second full-fidelity PII store outside the production trust boundary, so any warehouse misconfiguration, backup, extract, dashboard or BI export leaks contactable customer records that could have been tokenised or hashed.",
      "component": "Nightly export job transformation",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "A nightly job copies the customers table, including email addresses, phone numbers and purchase history, into the analytics warehouse." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-359", "CWE-212"],
      "plainLanguage": "The export copies real emails and phone numbers when analysts probably only need anonymous data, doubling the places PII can leak from.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Minimise and mask identifiers in the analytics copy",
        "given": "the nightly export builds the analytics customers dataset",
        "when": "a column contains a direct identifier such as email or phone",
        "then": "it is excluded, tokenised or masked unless a documented analytics use case requires the raw value"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Warehouse copy bypasses the application's own access controls on customer records",
      "scenario": "In the application, customer records are presumably protected by role and tenant checks. The exported copy sits behind only the warehouse's flat analyst grant, so a user who could never see another customer's purchase history in the product can read it in the warehouse. The export effectively promotes read privileges for everyone with warehouse access.",
      "component": "Production to warehouse trust boundary",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "copies the customers table" },
        { "quote": "All analysts have read access to the warehouse." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-285"],
      "plainLanguage": "Data that is locked down in the app becomes wide open once it is copied into the warehouse.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Carry production authorization constraints into the warehouse",
        "given": "customer data is protected by role or tenant rules in the application",
        "when": "the same data is exported to the warehouse",
        "then": "equivalent authorization constraints are enforced in the warehouse before any analyst can query it"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "A compromised export job can silently corrupt or redirect the customer dataset",
      "scenario": "The nightly job holds read credentials for the production customers table and write credentials for the warehouse. An attacker who compromises the job host or its credentials can read the whole customer base on demand, write falsified rows that skew business reporting, or point the export at a destination they control. Nothing in the design verifies the integrity or destination of each run.",
      "component": "Nightly export job and its credentials",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "A nightly job copies the customers table" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-522"],
      "plainLanguage": "The nightly job has the keys to all customer data; whoever controls the job controls that data and the reports built on it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Harden and scope the export job credentials and destination",
        "given": "the nightly export job runs with database and warehouse credentials",
        "when": "it executes",
        "then": "it uses least-privilege, rotated credentials from a secret store, writes only to a fixed allow-listed destination, and each run records a verifiable row count and checksum"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Deleted or opted-out customers keep living in the warehouse copy",
      "scenario": "Because the job copies the customers table nightly with no stated retention or propagation rules, records a customer asked to erase, or data past its retention period, persist in warehouse tables, snapshots and derived extracts. Analysts keep querying contact details and purchase history the business no longer has a right to hold, which is both a privacy breach and a regulatory exposure.",
      "component": "Analytics warehouse retention",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "A nightly job copies the customers table, including email addresses, phone numbers and purchase history, into the analytics warehouse." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-212"],
      "plainLanguage": "If a customer asks to be deleted, their details can stay in the analytics copy forever.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Propagate deletion and retention to the analytics copy",
        "given": "a customer record is deleted or reaches its retention limit in production",
        "when": "the next nightly export runs",
        "then": "the corresponding rows and derived extracts are removed from the warehouse within a defined window"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No way to tell which analyst read which customers' personal data",
      "scenario": "With a single shared read grant across all analysts and no described query attribution, an insider who bulk-exports customer contact details cannot be identified afterwards, and an accused analyst can plausibly deny it. During a suspected leak the team cannot scope which customers were actually exposed, which blocks breach notification decisions. This matters here because the dataset is bulk PII, not aggregate metrics.",
      "component": "Analyst query access to warehouse",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "All analysts have read access to the warehouse." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "If customer data leaks from the warehouse, nobody can prove who looked at it or which customers were affected.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Attribute and retain access records for PII queries",
        "given": "an analyst queries the exported customer dataset",
        "when": "the query touches identifier or purchase-history columns",
        "then": "the query, the named individual account and the rows returned are recorded in a tamper-resistant log that analysts cannot alter"
      }
    }
  ]
}
